title: ProTEA: Programmable Transformer Encoder Acceleration on FPGA
problem: Hardware accelerators for transformer encoder blocks are limited and inflexible, with most prior work targeting sparse architectures that cannot efficiently support the dense computations of popular transformer variants.
motivation: Transformers are widely adopted in NLP, machine translation, and computer vision, but lack specialized hardware accelerators for their core multi-head attention and feedforward blocks.
method: ProTEA implements a runtime programmable FPGA accelerator that uses efficient matrix tiling to distribute multi-head attention and feedforward computations across FPGA memory and computing resources. Deployed on Xilinx Alveo U55C, it employs tile sizes of 64 for attention operations and 6 for feedforward networks, configured for 8 parallel attention heads, 12 layers, and 768 embedding dimensions to maximize parallelism.
key_novelty: Runtime programmable matrix tiling approach that distributes dense transformer encoder computations across heterogeneous FPGA resources while maintaining architectural flexibility.
contributions: Runtime programmable FPGA accelerator for dense transformer encoder blocks
Efficient matrix tiling strategy for distributed multi-head attention and feedforward computation
Achieves 2.5× speedup versus NVIDIA Titan XP GPU
1.3-2.8× improvement over state-of-the-art custom FPGA accelerators

metrics.speedup: 2.5× vs NVIDIA Titan XP GPU; 1.3-2.8× vs state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators

primary_theme: Programmable FPGA acceleration for transformer encoders
